_comment: Per-platform capability matrix for oga-re. The purpose is that Hermes can ask THIS file how to unpack a game, which CPU architecture to use, which Ghidra loader applies, which emulator can supply runtime memory, and whether a matching decompilation already exists — instead of holding that knowledge per game. Every entry below was verified against the extension's own release assets, extension.properties/build.gradle, and the emulator's source or docs. 'research_needed' and 'no_maintained_tooling' are real answers, not placeholders.

statusLegend.ready: tooling identified AND a build exists for a Ghidra version we can install
statusLegend.partially_ready: tooling works but has a real caveat (abandoned upstream, young/thin bus factor, or a version mismatch needing a source build)
statusLegend.research_needed: not yet established; do not claim support
statusLegend.blocked_version_conflict: tooling exists but requires a Ghidra version incompatible with the rest of the workflow

ghidraVersionPlan._whyThisSectionExists: Extensions are compiled against a specific Ghidra release and the 11->12 jump broke pre-12 extensions hard (Ghidra issue #8976: NoSuchMethodError in ExtensionUtils). Two of the FE11 tools require versions no single install satisfies, so the split is tracked here rather than rediscovered later as a mysterious load failure.
ghidraVersionPlan.installedNow: Ghidra 12.1.3 PUBLIC (20260817) with Temurin JDK 21 — the modern line, and what every 'ready' platform below targets or is close to.
ghidraVersionPlan.requiredLater: Ghidra 11.2.1 must be installed MANUALLY from GitHub releases (scoop carries only 12.1.3; the versions bucket has only ghidra92) before dsd-ghidra symbol sync is attempted.
ghidraVersionPlan.conflict: dsd-ghidra v0.7.0 supports Ghidra 11.2.1 ONLY. NTRGhidra v1.5.1 requires 12.0.4. No single install satisfies both. PyGhidra did not exist before 11.3, so symbol sync on 11.2.1 cannot be headless at all — and dsd-ghidra's sync is GUI-only by construction (Swing file chooser, zero headless code paths).
ghidraVersionPlan.consequence: Two side-by-side Ghidra installs, never one reconciled install. Project data does NOT go backwards: a project touched in 12.x cannot be reopened by 11.2.1.
ghidraVersionPlan.onlyPlatformWithBothLines: ps1 — lab313ru/ghidra_psx_ldr ships a ghidra_11.2.1_PUBLIC build (2025.05.10) AND a 12.1.3 build (2026.09.03), so it is the only extension here that could live in either install.

nds.name: Nintendo DS
loaders: dsd-ghidra v0.7.0 (Ghidra 11.2.1) — dsd-aware: syncs functions, data symbols, sections, delinks, relocations, overlay/autoload mapping from a ds-decomp project
NTRGhidra v1.5.1 (Ghidra 12.0.4) — standalone ROM loader, adds dynamic overlay load/unload and bundled ARM9/ARM7 register labels + Function ID database

runtimeAccess.melonDS: in-process MainRAM pointer (used by the OGA harnesses); also has a debugger. No gdbstub needed for our reads.

nds.symbolInterchange: dsd-ghidra consumes the decomp project's config.yaml + symbols.txt directly. VERIFIED WORKING via OgaImportDsdSymbols.java: 1,495 names applied (1,026 functions, 469 data) — the program went from 3,774 functions / 0 named to 4,104 / 1,032 named.

matchingDecomp.licence: NONE — no LICENSE/COPYING, no SPDX headers, GitHub API license: null. Cite addresses and symbol NAMES with attribution; do NOT copy code, headers or config files.
matchingDecomp.modules: arm9 main + ITCM + DTCM autoloads + 12 ARM9 overlays (ov000-ov011). ARM7 NOT represented.
matchingDecomp.buildRequires: Python 3.11+, GCC 9+, Ninja, MetroWerks mwccarm 2.0/sp2p2 (auto-downloaded; run via Wibo/Wine off-Windows). `python tools/configure.py YFEE01 && ninja`.
matchingDecomp.completeness: ~15-20% and NOT an official match %: 20,982 symbol lines, 12,328 functions of which 10,559 are auto-named func_* and 1,769 carry real names.

blockers: dsd-ghidra requires Ghidra 11.2.1, which scoop does not carry — manual GitHub download needed.
dsd-ghidra's symbol sync is GUI-only; automating it needs a wrapper bypassing DsdConfigChooser to call dsdghidra.sync.* directly.
NTRGhidra needs 12.0.4 so it cannot coexist with dsd-ghidra in one install.

psp.name: PlayStation Portable
psp.cpu: Allegrex (MIPS32 R4000-class derivative + Allegrex-specific instructions + VFPU)
psp.ghidraNative: PARTIAL — Ghidra ships MIPS:LE:32:default but has no VFPU, no PSP ELF/PRX relocation types A/B, and no PSP calling convention. A decrypted EBOOT.PBP/PRX is not importable by stock Ghidra.
psp.loaderGhidraVersion: v21.4 (2026-08-25) is built for Ghidra 12.1.3 ONLY (CI matrix ['12.1.3']). Last multi-version release v21.2 (2025-03-23) ships zips for 11.2–11.4.3. NO 11.2.1 BUILD — only 11.2.

runtimeAccess.PPSSPP: Network WebSocket debugger at /debugger, subprotocol 'debugger.ppsspp.org'; enable with RemoteDebuggerOnStartup=true or --debugger=PORT (PPSSPPHeadless halts before running — ideal for pre-setting breakpoints). JSON messages with a 'ticket' for request/response correlation.
runtimeAccess.capabilities: memory.read_u8/u16/u32, memory.read, readString, writes; memory.search (Cheat-Engine style with wildcard mask); memory.disasm, searchDisasm, assemble; cpu.breakpoint/memory.breakpoint/regBreakpoint add/update/remove/list; async cpu.breakpoint.hit events INCLUDING LOG-ONLY breakpoints that never stop the CPU — this is what makes automation possible; hle.module.*, hle.backtrace; Tools/wsdbg/ Rust CLI client in the repo.

psp.symbolInterchange: STRONGEST OF ANY PLATFORM — BIDIRECTIONAL AND ALREADY BUILT. ghidra-allegrex ships PpssppImportSymFile (load PPSSPP .sym into Ghidra) and PpssppExportSymFile (export Ghidra labels back to .sym). Formats: NoCash-style .sym, .map, and the modern per-module .ppsym under PSP/SYSTEM/SYMBOLS/<module>_<crc>.ppsym.
psp.saveStateAnalysis: not established — .ppst is an opaque tagged chunk stream with no published spec. Treat as internal.
psp.notes: Strategically important for Dragon Ball Z: Shin Budokai Another Road. Two caveats worth recording: (1) installing the 11.2 build on 11.2.1 triggers Ghidra's version-mismatch dialog ('Install Anyway'); building v21.2 from source is the clean fix. (2) REGRESSION — 'PPSSPP debugger integration was removed' in v21 (2026-02-06) because Ghidra dropped Debugger framework support in 11.3, so the Ghidra-side live-debugger connector no longer exists in any release; live debugging must go through PPSSPP's own WebSocket API.

gba.name: Game Boy Advance
gba.ghidraNative: YES for the CPU (ARM:LE:32:v4t). Missing natively: ROM container handling and the memory-map/IO setup.
gba.loaderGhidraVersion: Explicit two-line split: v1.1.0 → Ghidra 12.0.2; v1.0.3 → Ghidra 11.4.3. README: 'For Ghidra 11 and older check the releases section or checkout from older commit as API was changed in Ghidra 12.' NO 11.2 or 11.2.1 build.
gba.emulator: mGBA (0.10.5 installed on this machine via scoop)

runtimeAccess.mGBA-lua: Built in since 0.10 (Tools > Scripting, Lua 5.4, documented at mgba.io/docs/scripting.html). Named MEMORY DOMAINS rather than a flat space (bios, ewram, iwram, io, palette, vram, oam, rom, sram), plus read8/16/32 + write8/16/32 by absolute address, register get/set, saveStateBuffer/File/Slot and load counterparts, loadFile, loadSaveFile, getGameTitle/getGameCode, addKey/getKeys/clearKeys, screenshots, console logging, currentFrame/frameCycles/frequency, callbacks (frame, reset, keysRead, savedataUpdated), reset/step/runFrame, and a raw TCP socket API.
runtimeAccess.mGBA-gdbstub: GBA ONLY, not GB (verified in src/gba/core.c vs src/gb/core.c — the GB core supports CUSTOM + CLI only). --debugGdb / -g, default port 2345, GDB Remote Serial Protocol with target.xml, memory-map XML, swbreak/hwbreak, Z/z types 0/1/2/3/4.
runtimeAccess.mGBA-cli: --debugCli gives break/dis, next, r/1|2|4, w/1|2|4, x/1|2|4, watch, and 'source <file>' to load external symbols. Reads No$GBA .sym including the trailing ,<length> variant.
runtimeAccess.symbolLoading: auto-loads an .elf beside the ROM with the same basename

gba.saveStateAnalysis: DOCUMENTED — src/gba/serialize.h and src/gb/serialize.h carry full byte-offset layouts (GB magic 0x00400003, sizeof 0x11800), exposed to Lua via saveStateBuffer.
gba.loaderMemoryMap: ROM 0x08000000 (init+exec), EWRAM 0x02000000 (256KB exec), IWRAM 0x03000000 (32KB exec), IO 0x04000000, PAL 0x05000000, VRAM 0x06000000 (96KB exec), OAM 0x07000000, SRAM 0x0E000000. RAM regions are declared UNINITIALIZED (correct for static RE) so the loader is static-analysis-only — pair it with mGBA's Lua/GDB for live RAM.
gba.notes: Strong target: Ghidra handles ARM/Thumb natively and mGBA's programmatic access is first-party and well documented. DEAD ALTERNATIVE — do not use SiD3W4y/GhidraGBA (last push 2021-12-13, bare ROM+RAM map, no header parsing); pudii is strictly better maintained. Also relevant to the OGA mGBA work: 0.10.5 has NO scripting breakpoints (those land in unreleased 0.11.0), which is why the compat shim emulates registerexec/registerwrite with per-frame polling.

gb.name: Game Boy
gb.cpu: Sharp SM83 (SoC is LR35902). NOT a Z80 — it drops Z80-only opcodes and redefines prefix handling, so Ghidra's built-in Z80 is not a usable substitute.
gb.ghidraNative: NO — Ghidra's processor list contains Z80 but NO SM83/LR35902 entry. A processor module is mandatory.
gb.loader: Gekkio/GhidraBoy — UPSTREAM ARCHIVED 2026-06-10. Best-maintained 12.x path is the community port ptthess/GhidraBoy-12.1.2-port.
gb.loaderGhidraVersion: Upstream final release 20250830 ships zips for 11.1–11.4.2 — NO 11.2.1 and NO 12.x. Community port tag 12.1.2 ships ghidra_12.1.2_PUBLIC_20260701_GhidraBoy.zip.
gb.loaderLastActivity: upstream last commit 2025-08-30, repo archived 2026-06-10; port released 2026-07-01 (1 star, single release)
gb.emulator: SameBoy (best debugger surface); BGB and Emulicious are strong alternatives

runtimeAccess.mGBA: works for GB/GBC but its GB core deliberately has NO GDB stub (CUSTOM + CLI debugger types only).
runtimeAccess.SameBoy: textual debugger with banked expressions/breakpoints; <rom>.sym and registers.sym auto-loaded; sameboy_debugger.exe; GB_set_async_input_callback for programmatic input.
runtimeAccess.BGB: headless /br/-wp/-stateonexit automation plus the shared no$gmb/BGB debug message protocol (Emulicious-compatible).
runtimeAccess.Emulicious: remote debugging TCP server + VS Code DAP, .sym/.cdb symbols.

gb.addressModelNote: BANKED. A 16-bit address does NOT identify code without its bank — the same address exists in every bank. GhidraBoy's own README lists banked 0x4000-0x7fff calls as needing MANUAL bank resolution, so this is a live limitation, not a theoretical one. This is why the common address model carries `bank` as a separate field.
gb.notes: Upstream abandonment is the risk: the only maintained path is a 1-star community port. The emulator side is the healthy half.

gbc.name: Game Boy Color
gbc.ghidraNative: NO — same as GB, no SM83 entry in stock Ghidra.
gbc.emulator: SameBoy / BGB / Emulicious; mGBA works but its GB core has no GDB stub
gbc.addressModelNote: Banked, plus ROM and RAM banking. Same bank:address requirement as GB.
gbc.notes: Shares every characteristic of gb. Listed separately because the platform manifest keys on it and because ROM/RAM banking behaviour differs at the CGB level.

nes.name: Nintendo Entertainment System
nes.ghidraNative: yes — Ghidra ships 6502 and 65C02 (Ghidra/Processors/6502/data/languages/6502.ldefs declares exactly those two)
nes.addressModelNote: Banked via mapper switching. Same bank-awareness problem as GB/SNES.
nes.notes: Deliberately deprioritised per the brief unless the tooling work proves reusable for banked-memory systems generally. The iNES/NES 2.0 container and mapper handling were not researched.

snes.name: Super Nintendo / Super Famicom
snes.cpu: Ricoh 5A22 = WDC 65C816 (24-bit banked addressing) + SPC700 audio CPU
snes.ghidraNative: NO native 65C816 — stock Ghidra's 6502 module declares only 6502:LE:16:default and 65C02:LE:16:default. No 65816, no 24-bit banked space.
snes.loaderGhidraVersion: gradle.properties: plugin.version=1.3.2, plugin.ghidraCompatibility=12.0.4; CI installs Ghidra 12.0.4 + JDK 21. Modern line — no third requirement introduced.
snes.loaderLastActivity: 2026-05-28 (~3.5 months idle as of verification), repo created 2026-05-01, 81 stars, single contributor
snes.emulator: Mesen 2 primary; bsnes-plus secondary for SA-1/SuperFX debugging

runtimeAccess.Mesen2: Lua API (emu.read/emu.write with memory-type enums, addMemoryCallback for read/write/exec ranges, addEventCallback, emu.log) PLUS a C DLL debug API (InitializeDebugger/GetProgramCounter/ResumeExecution) so external tools can drive it. Symbol import/export: .mlb, WLA-DX .sym, .cdb, .dbg, .fns, ELF, with the debug workspace as a documented JSON file.
runtimeAccess.bsnes-plus: reads WLA/asar .sym auto-loaded from the ROM's directory; adds SA-1/SuperFX disassembly.

snes.addressModelNote: Banked with LoROM/HiROM/ExHiROM mappings plus enhancement chips. A logical address is meaningless without its mapping and bank context.
snes.notes: Hardware coverage is genuinely good (LoROM, HiROM, ExHiROM, SA-1, GSU/SuperFX, CX-4, DSP-n, OBC1 fully supported with canon + mirror banks, score-based header detection, checksum validation). Why not 'ready': cart support is explicitly PARTIAL for S-DD1 and SPC7110, the repo is ~4.5 months old with one contributor and no activity since 2026-05-28 — a young, thin-bus-factor dependency rather than a battle-tested one. Pin to Ghidra 12.0.4.

genesis.name: Sega Genesis / Mega Drive
genesis.ghidraNative: YES for the CPU that matters — Ghidra ships 68000:BE:32:default, MC68020, MC68030, and Z80 is also built in. Missing natively: ROM header parsing, the 68000 memory map (ROM 0x000000, Z80 window 0xA00000, I/O 0xA10000), vector-table setup, VDP/IO register definitions.
genesis.loaderGhidraVersion: OLD — Ghidra 11.0.1. Release v2.3 (2024-03-09) is literally titled 'Updated to Ghidra 11.0.1'. Pre-11.2 and pre-12.x. This is the only OLD-line dependency in this matrix.
genesis.loaderLastActivity: 2024-03-09 — ~2.5 years stale. Fork DohmBoy64Bit/ghidra_sega_ldr has one 2026-06-20 commit, no releases, unverified.
genesis.emulator: BlastEm (gdbstub + CLI debugger) primary; Exodus secondary for VDP-level work; MAME Lua for the Z80 side

runtimeAccess.BlastEm: acts as a GDB remote stub — 'blastem ROM.bin -D' listens on port 1234, then 'target remote :1234' from m68k-elf-gdb with the matching ELF for symbols; halts at entry so breakpoints can be preset. Documented limitations: NO watchpoints, NO tracepoints. Integrated CLI debugger with b/d, co, step/next/bt, p/di, vs/vr (VDP), zb/zp (Z80).
runtimeAccess.Exodus: documented C++ plugin SDK; exodus-mcp-extension wraps it as HTTP/JSON-RPC on localhost:8600 with read/write memory, disassemble, search, breakpoints, bus-level watchpoints, step_device, plus VRAM/CRAM/VSRAM/VDP registers.
runtimeAccess.MAME: Lua debugger (-debug) with bpset/bplist, wpset, symbols:memory_value for 68K and Z80 devices.

genesis.saveStateAnalysis: not established — save states are emulator-internal, no documented versioned format for analysis input.
genesis.notes: SPLIT VERDICT, recorded honestly: the CPU is natively supported, so useful disassembly/decompilation of a Genesis ROM is achievable today with a plain raw import plus a small headless script to map ROM/Z80/VDP regions and apply reset vectors — no third-party extension needed. What is missing is maintained loader polish. Practical guidance: use built-in 68000:BE:32 on the modern install; keep the old loader only as an optional legacy-install convenience.

n64.name: Nintendo 64
n64.cpu: NEC VR4300i (MIPS III, big-endian, TLB-mapped) + RSP + RDP
n64.ghidraNative: PARTIAL — generic MIPS modules cover the VR4300 instruction set and the ELF loader can load N64 ELFs. Missing: ROM container/byte-order handling, RDRAM/ROM/PIF boot memory map, IPL3/entry-point logic, RSP microcode language.
n64.loaderGhidraVersion: Maintained release-per-Ghidra-version: 'Extension for Ghidra 12.1.2' (2026-08-01), 12.1, 12.0.4 (2026-03-29), 12.0, plus older 11.4.1/11.3.x/11.1.x. A 12.0.4 build exists so it can share the modern install. NOT old.
n64.loaderLastActivity: 2026-08-01, 167 stars, tracks every Ghidra point release
n64.emulator: ares (N64 core with a built-in GDB server) primary; mupen64plus debugger API secondary

runtimeAccess.ares: implements a GDB server (ares/n64/system/system.cpp registers GDB::server.hooks with targetXML '<architecture>mips:4000</architecture>' and a devirtualizeDebug hook so GDB can use virtual addresses) — any GDB client can attach, step, breakpoint and read VRAM/RDRAM.
runtimeAccess.mupen64plus: first-class Core Debugger API (DebugGetCPUDataPtr/DebugMemGetPointer, DEBUGGER build flag, interpreter CPU); RMG is a fork with a Qt6 WebSocket bridge + Python MCP server exposing read/write_rdram, MIPS register r/w, translate_address, disassemble, breakpoints/watchpoints, .map symbols and JSONL instruction traces.

n64.symbolInterchange: Splat takes a YAML config plus symbol_addrs.txt ('name = 0x801378C0; // type:func size:0x10 rom:0x6E75FC segment:my_overlay'), splits/segments the ROM (header, IPL3, code/dat/rodata, overlays where rom:/segment: disambiguate symbols sharing a VRAM address), and writes the linker script. blackgamma7/n64_ghidra supplies syncSplatSymbols (round-trip Ghidra symbols back into splat format), exportSymbolPJ64 and an N64 OS .gdt type archive. N64LoaderWV consumes N64sym/address-name or byte-pattern signatures.
n64.addressModelNote: ROM byte order varies — .z64 big-endian, .n64 little-endian, .v64 byte-swapped — all handled by N64LoaderWV's endianness fix. Code is loaded from overlays; where Splat already segments, integrate rather than rediscover.

ps1.name: PlayStation 1
ps1.ghidraNative: PARTIAL — Ghidra has MIPS but no R3000-specific module (mips.ldefs lists default/16e/R6/micro, and the generic MIPS:LE:32:default is what community guidance says to use). The gap is executable-format handling: PS-X EXE carries an explicit load address, and overlays load dynamically.
ps1.loaderGhidraVersion: 2026.09.03 → Ghidra 12.1.3; 2026.01.04 → final 11.x INCLUDING 11.4.3; and the 2025.05.10 release includes ghidra_11.2.1_PUBLIC_20250510_ghidra_psx_ldr.zip. THE ONLY EXTENSION IN THIS MATRIX WITH A 11.2.1 BUILD AND A 12.1.3 BUILD.
ps1.loaderLastActivity: 2026-09-03, 331 stars, 20 contributors, 69 releases — one of the most actively developed here

runtimeAccess.DuckStation: GDB Remote Serial Protocol (src/core/gdb_server.cpp, mips:3000 target.xml, Z/z types 0-4, MAX_WATCHPOINT_LENGTH 256), enable via the 'Enable GDB Server' debugging setting, default port 2345, enabled on all platforms except Android. Also 'Export Shared Memory' maps guest RAM to duckstation_<...> for external readers. NOTE: the PINE IPC server was dropped.
runtimeAccess.PCSX-Redux: GDB server on 3333 and a Lua API with PCSX.addBreakpoint(invoker callbacks), getMemPtr, getRegisters.

ps1.symbolInterchange: community PSX-EXE→ELF converters and PsyQ .SYM handling exist (This Dust Remembers, psx_psyq_signatures); the loader itself handles PSYQ LIB/OBJ marker files and a GTE macro segment.
ps1.notes: The only platform that can live in EITHER Ghidra install, which makes it useful for validating the two-install setup. Community guidance: use MIPS:LE:32:default (not R3000) and base 0x80010000 for a PS-X EXE.

ps2.name: PlayStation 2
ps2.cpu: Emotion Engine R5900 (MIPS III + 128-bit MMI + VU0 macro mode COP2) + R3000A IOP + VU0/VU1 micro
ps2.ghidraNative: NO — generic MIPS modules exist but there is no EE language: no MMI instructions, no VU0 macro-mode COP2, no EE register set/CSRs, no .mdebug/SNDLL recovery, no PCSX2 save-state import.
ps2.loaderGhidraVersion: v2.1.37 (2026-08-25) adds Ghidra 12.1.3; v2.1.36/35 shipped 12.0.1-12.1.2 zips; v2.1.34 (2026-03-07) shipped 11.4.1-11.4.3. A 12.0.4 build exists, so it can share the modern install with NDS/N64/SNES tooling. NOT old.

runtimeAccess.PCSX2-debugger: Debug > Open Debugger (needs Tools > Show Advanced Settings) with R5900 (EE) and R3000 (IOP) layouts, breakpoints, memory search, function stubbing, expression evaluator.
runtimeAccess.PCSX2-symbols: .sym text files ('<addr> <name>[:<size>]' plus .asc/.byt/.wrd/.dbl directives) and ELF .symtab/.strtab, MIPS .mdebug and SNDLL .sndata tables (since v2.1.113) via a SymbolDatabase/CCC importer.
runtimeAccess.PCSX2-savestate: IMPORTED DIRECTLY INTO GHIDRA by the EE-reloaded extension as analysis input. CAVEAT: modern PCSX2 default zstd compression must be switched to Deflate64 (File > Settings > Advanced > Savestate Settings) or SavestateZstdCompression=false, else Ghidra's zip reader reports 'unsupported method'.
runtimeAccess.PINE: built-in TCP/Unix-socket IPC (EmuCore/EnablePINE=true, default slot/port 28011) for reading/writing EE memory and triggering savestate save/load. Reference clients: GovanifY/pine, C0mposer/PCSX2-Memory-Accessor, dmang-dev/mcp-pine.
runtimeAccess.PCSX2-gdb: NOT IN MAINLINE — verified against the current tree; needs a fork (mdecicco/pcsx2-gdb last push 2021, vertver/pcsx2-gdbserver, snowyegret23/PCSX2_MCP which requires a custom build). Treat GDB-attach as unverified/DIY.

ps2.notes: Best-supported of the eight. Strategically important for Dragon Ball Z: Budokai 3 and the Budokai Tenkaichi titles. Caveats: (a) the extension tracks Ghidra releases 1:1, so pin exactly; (b) decompilation of some functions fails with 'Decompiler Parameter ID' enabled (documented workaround: disable it); (c) GNU demangling of .mdebug names needs 'Use Deprecated Demangler'; (d) VU1 micro code and IOP-side work are not covered by the language module (VU0 macro mode is).

deferred._comment: Evaluated later. Listed so intent is recorded without implying tooling exists. Deliberately deprioritised so future platform exploration does not distract from FE11 and the mGBA work.

summary._caveat: No platform is claimed as VERIFIED WORKING on this machine except nds, where an ARM9 import, analysis, symbol sync and structure queries have actually been executed. The rest are 'tooling identified and a compatible build exists'.
